chapter: Arthur Gibbs, Savoy Ballroom and recording sessions
title: Arthur Gibbs's band at the Savoy and Colonnades: personnel
summary: Caldwell played tenor in Arthur Gibbs's ten-piece band, with Billy Taylor, Sammy Hodges and Edgar Sampson; Gibbs wrote Running Wild.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Because they've got you down (unintelligible) with Arthur Peterson (unintelligible) summer of '27 and '28.
That's right. He's --
Where was that?
Savoy Ballroom. Then we left the Savoy Ballroom and went down to the -- to the big ballroom on Broadway. It's not there now. They tore it -- they closed it up about seven --
Colonnades?
Colonnades, yeah. And they had three bandstands few grandstands, and we left the Savoy, went down to the Colonnade.
Oh, who was in that band?
Well, we had -- Ovie Alston Guy Ross was on trumpet.
Oh, the guy that went with Claude Hopeton.
With Claude Hopeton (unintelligible) Billy Taylor was on bass. Sammy Hodges on drums -- no relation to Johnny Hodges -- Paul Bernett was on (banjo) (unintelligible).
Sammy Hodges?
Yeah.
Never heard of him.
Yeah, good drummer and good arranger, not related to Johnny Hodges at all, and we had Cliff on tenor -- on trumpet -- fine trumpet player.
Who?
Cliff Worthington on trumpet. And George Washington on trombone.
Oh, he was a pretty trombone player.
Yeah, we had Gene Michael on alto. His brother (Unintelligible) was on third alto, and I was on tenor, and Billy Taylor was on bass. Arthur Gibb was on piano. We had ten pieces.
-- piano player was opposite you?
Good piano player, good musician, he the one that wrote 'Running Wild' for the 'Running Wild' show.
Oh, yeah?
He composed that.
Was he like Fats or --
Very -- he's a varied -- type of a musician, varied the depth and reading and all.
